question.text: Under the SEBI SAST (Takeover) Regulations, when listed securities of the acquirer are offered to the target's shareholders as the mode of payment in an open offer (as summarised at p.199 of the NISM-Series-IX workbook), the relevant date for determining the pricing of those securities is best described as:

answer.text: The date of the acquirer's board meeting approving the open offer
The date 30 days prior to the relevant general meeting of the acquirer's shareholders
The date of the relevant general meeting itself
The date of allotment of the consideration shares

explanation.text: The Logic: The NISM-Series-IX workbook, p.199, sets out the SAST payment-mode rule that where the acquirer offers its own listed securities as consideration in an open offer, those securities are priced with reference to a date 30 days prior to the relevant general meeting of the acquirer's shareholders. With the stem now explicitly framed around the p.199 SAST rule, the unique correct answer is the 30-day-prior date. The Trap: The board-meeting date is the relevant date in other SEBI ICDR contexts (e.g., QIPs at p.171, and non-SPA preferential issues). The "date of the general meeting itself" and "date of allotment" do not correspond to any pricing reference date under SAST p.199. In the audit-flagged original wording (which referenced an "SPA-based preferential issue"), the 30-day-prior rule was not directly supported on the preferential-issue pages (pp.166-169), so candidates could legitimately argue for the board-meeting date instead. Note: The original stem mixed two contexts — preferential issue and SAST — without anchoring either, and used the unclear abbreviation "SPA". The stem has been retargeted to the p.199 SAST payment-mode rule, where the 30-day-prior date is directly supported in the workbook, making the keyed answer unambiguous.
